sections.title: The Failure of Traditional Dimensions
lecture_lines: Points, lines, planes, and cubes exist.
But what about rough, self-similar objects?
animations: Display Euclidean 1D Line and 2D Square at center in #FFFFFF.
Highlight the line and square with scaling growth effect.
Fade in complex coastline silhouette in #FF00FF.
Contrast traditional geometry label with fractal coastline label.
Show equation D = log(N)/log(s) in center #00FFFF.

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Power Law of Scaling
lecture_lines: Scaling by 1/s grows pieces by N.
Relationship follows: N equals s to power D.
Fractal dimension D is log N over log s.
animations: Display equation N = s^D in #FFFF00 at center.
Animate scale factor 's' growing from 1 to 3.
Show count of parts 'N' scaling exponentially based on 's'.

sections.title: Calculating the Fractal Dimension: The Koch Snowflake
lecture_lines: Koch snowflakes begin with a straight line.
Replace segments with four, one-third length.
Calculation yields: D equals log 4 over log 3.
Result is approximately one point two six.
animations: Draw initial triangle line segment in #00FF00.
Show replacing 1 segment with 4 segments (s=3, N=4).
Indicate self-similarity through recursive iteration animation.
Display calculation formula: D = log(4) / log(3).
Finalize full Koch Snowflake geometry in #00FF00.

sections.title: Application in Nature and Technology
lecture_lines: Human lungs maximize oxygen exchange surface.
Fractal antennas optimize smartphone signal reception.
animations: Show visual of human lung structure in #00FFFF.
Highlight branching fractal nature of lung airways.
Animate smartphone antenna signal waves in #FFFF00.
